channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: DeepTutor: your own AI tutor that remembers what you are learning
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: DeepTutor (HKUDS/DeepTutor, Apache-2.0, roughly 48,000 stars) is an agent-native learning workspace that remembers what you are learning across sessions. We installed 1.7.0 from PyPI, wired it to a free local Qwen3 model through Ollama, and ran a real chat explanation and quiz — no account, no API key, no GPU — with the small model's mistakes quoted honestly.

item.title: DOJ is asking whether Nvidia's $12.93B Hugging Face deal would capture a key distribution point for AI
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: The Justice Department is asking whether Nvidia's $12.93 billion purchase of Hugging Face would hand the chipmaker control of a key distribution point for AI — the latest turn in a years-long antitrust probe of Nvidia's conduct.

item.title: A 4B model read one sentence and fetched a netherite ingot from bare hands
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A 1:58 split-screen clip shows a tiny local decision model turning one plain-language Minecraft request into a full bare-hands run — porkchops and a netherite ingot. The maker is candid about what the model didn’t do, and Reddit’s sharpest comments say so too.

item.title: RBC blocks AI agents from online banking: Canada's biggest bank draws a line on agentic AI
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada has cut third-party personal AI agents off from its online banking, calling the risk to customers unacceptable — the first Canadian bank to do so, and the latest sign that banks will decide for themselves how far agents get into your money.

item.title: Archon: make your AI coding agents deterministic — hands-on with the open-source harness builder
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Archon (coleam00/Archon, MIT) turns your agent process into a YAML graph — steps, checks, and human gates the engine runs the same way every time. We installed CLI v0.13.0, validated and ran two bash-only workflows with no account, no key, and no model, and put an approval gate between a check and a release — all verified, with the paid provider step clearly marked.

item.title: Smolagents: the agent that thinks in Python code, running on a local model with no API key
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Smolagents turns an agent into Python code: the model writes a program, a sandboxed interpreter runs it, and your tools answer what the model does not know. We built a CodeAgent on Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct running locally — one hand-written tool, two tasks, no API key — and report all four runs that failed before the finishing instructions made it work.

item.title: UK Autumn Budget confirms the AI package: a Sovereign AI Unit, a data-centre covenant, and £500M for safety and security
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Chancellor John Healey used his Autumn Budget speech to confirm the UK AI spending push: about £500M for safety and security, a Sovereign AI Unit backed by £140M, and a data-centre covenant trading grid access for community commitments. The money is real; the statute behind it is not yet.

item.title: A robot arm painted three fish from a single chat — and Reddit argued over whether the video was even real
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: A 17-second split-screen clip of a robot arm painting three fish has r/singularity split between awe and suspicion. The maker answered the loudest objection with raw footage — and a candid account of what the model actually controlled.

item.title: MetaHarness: mint your own branded agent harness — scaffold, validate, and ship it under your name
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Cognitum One announced MetaHarness at GitHub Universe on October 28, 2026: a factory that scaffolds a branded agent harness — its own CLI, MCP server, agents, and default-deny policy — under your name. We scaffolded two harnesses, ran their doctor gates, tests, MCP handshake, and repo scorecard, all with no account, no API key, and no GPU.

item.title: Anthropic asks California for court power to block risky AI models, and argues against a blanket kill switch
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: In an October 15 letter to Governor Gavin Newsom, Anthropic asked California to let officials seek a court order blocking the release of a model found to pose a serious risk — while warning that a mandatory kill switch for entire models would give regulators false comfort.

item.title: PhotoCraft: the open-source Photoshop rival you can drive from the terminal
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: PhotoCraft is a clean-room Photoshop rebuild in pure Rust with 74,000 GitHub stars — and its headless CLI edits real images without opening a window. We downloaded v0.17.0, ran its sharpen, curves, batch, convert, and MCP commands, and graded a folder of photos with one recipe file. No account, no API key, no GPU.

item.title: Google DeepMind launches Gemini 4 Carbon: its strongest model yet, built for cyber defense — but almost nobody can use it yet
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Google DeepMind’s second Gemini 4 model tops the revised Artificial Analysis index at 59 and leads key cybersecurity benchmarks, but it is rolling out first to a small group of cyber defenders — with no date for everyone else.

item.title: A working RISC-V CPU now runs inside a language model's weights — no silicon, no sandbox, no external runtime
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A 13-second screen recording of a language model doing arithmetic on a CPU compiled into its own weights has r/LocalLLaMA buzzing. The computer is real, open, and deterministic — but the thread's verdict is more measured than the headline: a brilliant stunt, not yet a useful machine.

item.title: Anatomy turns your coding agent into an illustrator: build interactive isometric figures that explain how things work
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Anatomy is a 21,500-star agent skill that explains ideas by building working isometric machines instead of boxes-and-arrows diagrams. Install it, build a shipped figure in under a second, and prompt your agent for figures that explain how things work — no API key for the install and the example build.

item.title: Rime launches Prism, a fine-tunable speech-to-speech model that checks its words before it speaks
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Rime launched Prism on October 28, 2026, a speech-to-speech model companies can fine-tune on their own calls and run on their own infrastructure — and it writes out its reply as text first, so a company's guardrails can vet every word before a caller hears it.

item.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe: one open-weight model for 40-language transcription, translation, and speaker labels
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe on October 28, 2026, an open-weight, promptable speech model that transcribes 40 languages, translates 31 to or from English, and labels up to eight speakers — alongside Granary v2, an open speech-data pipeline covering 463,062 hours across 48 languages.

item.title: Ruflo: the 80,000-star agent harness, installed and verified — swarms, local memory, and an MCP server you can actually run
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Ruflo wraps Claude Code and Codex in a harness of swarms, memory, and 379 MCP tools. We installed version 3.63.7, scaffolded a project, and stored and retrieved a decision from local vector memory — no API key. Here is the whole verified path, plus the honest limits.

item.title: AvalonX emerges from stealth with up to $10M: AI pen-testing for small businesses that attackers test least
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: AvalonX launched Artemis on October 28, 2026, pairing a 400-billion-parameter security AI trained on nine years of offensive-security data with human testers — backed by up to $10 million from Ridown Capital — to bring continuous penetration testing to small and midsize businesses.

item.title: Harvey clears the federal bar: FedRAMP Class D opens U.S. government legal work to its AI
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Harvey announced FedRAMP Class D certification on October 28, 2026, letting U.S. federal agencies, contractors and partners use its legal AI inside Knox Systems' certified cloud environment — the same platform used by 80% of the Am Law 100.

item.title: Fragment launches with $56M to automate the procurement work enterprise software leaves behind
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Fragment came out of stealth on October 28, 2026 with $56 million in funding and a pitch aimed at the messiest corner of enterprise software: the purchasing and payment exceptions that big manufacturers and distributors still resolve by hand.

item.title: Ask for a poster like you'd ask a designer: a hands-on guide to LangChain's design agent
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: LangChain's design agent (langchain-ai/design-agent, Apache-2.0, 183 GitHub stars) is the open-source Content Studio agent: a Deep Agents agent that turns a Slack thread or a terminal prompt into on-brand stills, decks, diagrams, charts and motion graphics, checking colours, fonts, contrast and chart math in code on every render. This guide runs its no-key Docker demo, asks it for a real LinkedIn card, and builds your own brand pack — then deploys it to Slack.

item.title: Upwind raises $400M at a $3.8B valuation to secure cloud and AI infrastructure
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Upwind Security announced a $400M Series C on October 28, 2026, led by Bessemer Venture Partners, valuing the cloud and AI security company at $3.8 billion — more than double its January valuation — as revenue quadrupled in 2026.

item.title: NVIDIA's 15,000-FPS MotionBricks is open source — and Reddit can't agree on how new that is
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A 42-second clip of an AI-driven game character sprinting through a sunlit courtyard has r/accelerate arguing about what “just open-sourced” means. The code is real, public, and Apache-licensed — but the footage is NVIDIA's summer demo, and the thread is split on the timeline.

item.title: Build a tool-calling agent that runs entirely on your laptop: LangGraph and a local Qwen model, no API key
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: LangGraph turns an agent into a graph you can inspect: nodes, edges, and a router that decides what runs next. This guide builds that graph around Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct running on your own CPU, gives it a calculator and a notes lookup, and proves the whole loop — tool calls, multi-step questions, and memory across turns — with no API key and no inference-time cloud call.

item.title: Meta's Muse lands in Singapore: Agoda becomes its first regional travel connector
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Meta launched its personal AI agent Muse in Singapore on October 28, 2026, with Agoda as the first travel platform regionally to connect its AI travel assistant — letting users in Singapore and Japan discover destinations, book hotels and manage itineraries in conversation.
